deck_name: よつばと！ Volumes 1–5 — Difficult Vocabulary for N3 Learners
source: あずまきよひこ「よつばと！」第1巻〜第5巻（電撃コミックス）
notes: Vocabulary drawn from Yotsuba&! volumes 1–5 that is likely to trip up an N3 learner. The manga uses highly colloquial, child-directed speech, heavy onomatopoeia, and casual contractions not often taught in textbooks. This deck targets: (1) words written in kanji that N3 learners may not recognise, (2) colloquial grammar words and sentence-final particles, (3) onomatopoeia that carry emotional or physical nuance, and (4) everyday words whose readings are deceptively tricky. Words well within N4–N3 range are excluded.

priority_guide.high: Learn first — appears frequently and blocks comprehension of whole exchanges.
priority_guide.medium: Learn after high priority — enriches understanding; context often helps.
priority_guide.low: Passive recognition is enough — look up once, don't drill.

difficulty_guide.at_level: Should be within N3 reach — worth solidifying.
difficulty_guide.one_above: N2 territory — challenging but worth the effort.
difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 territory — ambitious; focus on reading first.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common and readable even at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may be unfamiliar — learn the reading carefully.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Kanji are obscure or complex — focus on kana reading first.

cards.simpler_synonym: 移動（いどう）※ニュアンス違い
cards.context: The manga opens with Yotsuba moving into a new neighbourhood. This word and its verb form 引っ越す appear in the very first pages and recur throughout volume 1.
cards.example_sentence: きのう引っ越してきたよつばです！
cards.example_reading: きのう ひっこして きた よつばです！
cards.example_meaning: I'm Yotsuba — I moved in yesterday!

cards.context: Used when Yotsuba or Koiwai introduce themselves to the Ayase family next door. The polite prefix ご is important for understanding register.
cards.example_sentence: ご近所に挨拶に行こう。
cards.example_reading: ごきんじょ に あいさつ に いこう。
cards.example_meaning: Let's go introduce ourselves to the neighbours.

cards.simpler_synonym: あいさつ（kana alone is fine）
cards.context: The kanji for 挨拶 are notoriously difficult and rarely written even by native speakers. Recognise the word by sound; don't stress about writing the kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 引っ越しの挨拶をする。
cards.example_reading: ひっこし の あいさつ を する。
cards.example_meaning: To pay a moving-in greeting visit.

meanings: sorry to bother you (said when entering someone's home)
cards.simpler_synonym: 入ります（いります）※丁寧さが違う
cards.context: Said every time a character enters the Ayase house. If you don't know this phrase you will be confused by a sentence with no obvious literal meaning.
cards.example_sentence: お邪魔します！と言ってから家に入った。
cards.example_reading: おじゃまします！ と いって から いえ に はいった。
cards.example_meaning: She said 'excuse me for intruding!' and then entered the house.

cards.context: A very common expression in casual Japanese that N3 learners often see but mis-parse. Also appears as しょうがない in the manga.
cards.example_sentence: 雨が降ってきた。仕方ないね。
cards.example_reading: あめ が ふって きた。しかたない ね。
cards.example_meaning: It started raining. Oh well, nothing we can do.

cards.context: Characters use this frequently in exasperated or matter-of-fact replies. Yanda and Jumbo use it a lot when Yotsuba asks naive questions.
cards.example_sentence: 当たり前だろ！知ってるよ！
cards.example_reading: あたりまえ だろ！しってるよ！
cards.example_meaning: Of course! I know that!

cards.context: Yotsuba finds everything mysterious and wonderful — this word captures her worldview. It appears both as a な-adjective (不思議な) and as a noun.
cards.example_sentence: よつばは不思議な子だな。
cards.example_reading: よつば は ふしぎ な こ だな。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba is a mysterious/curious kid, isn't she.

cards.context: Used by adult characters to describe Yotsuba's honest, uncomplicated nature. Contrasts with more 'knowing' children.
cards.example_sentence: よつばは素直でいい子だ。
cards.example_reading: よつば は すなお で いい こ だ。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba is an honest, good girl.

meanings: person who has lost their way
cards.context: Appears in the amusement park volume when Yotsuba gets separated. The kanji combination 迷子 is a fixed compound — the reading まいご is not predictable from the individual kanji readings.
cards.example_sentence: よつばが迷子になった！
cards.example_reading: よつば が まいご に なった！
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba got lost!

cards.context: Yotsuba makes and reports promises constantly. Included because N3 learners sometimes still mix up the kanji reading.
cards.example_sentence: じゃあ約束だよ！明日また来るからね。
cards.example_reading: じゃあ やくそく だよ！あした また くる から ね。
cards.example_meaning: OK it's a promise! I'll come again tomorrow.

meanings: wooden corridor/platform along the edge of a traditional Japanese house
cards.simpler_synonym: テラス（ただし縁側は日本式）
cards.context: The Ayase house has a traditional 縁側 where characters sit and chat. The word is culturally important for understanding scene-setting in classic Japanese homes.
cards.example_sentence: おばあちゃんは縁側に座って庭を見ていた。
cards.example_reading: おばあちゃん は えんがわ に すわって にわ を みていた。
cards.example_meaning: Grandma was sitting on the veranda looking at the garden.

cards.context: Koiwai and the Ayase sisters use this constantly when ordering Yotsuba to clean up or when tidying after activities.
cards.example_sentence: 遊んだあとはちゃんと片付けること！
cards.example_reading: あそんだ あとは ちゃんと かたづける こと！
cards.example_meaning: Make sure you tidy up properly after playing!

cards.context: Appears in domestic scenes. N3 learners often know this word in hiragana but struggle to recognise the kanji quickly in manga panels.
cards.example_sentence: よつばもお父さんの洗濯を手伝った。
cards.example_reading: よつば も おとうさん の せんたく を てつだった。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba helped her dad with the laundry too.

cards.context: Yotsuba insists on helping with everything. This verb recurs constantly. The ず→う verb conjugation trips up learners.
cards.example_sentence: よつばも手伝う！
cards.example_reading: よつば も てつだう！
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba will help too!

cards.simpler_synonym: ベッド（ただし布団は日本式）
cards.context: Appears in morning scenes and sleep-over sequences. The kanji 布団 have unusual readings and are worth memorising as a pair.
cards.example_sentence: 布団を干さないといけないな。
cards.example_reading: ふとん を ほさない と いけない な。
cards.example_meaning: I really should air out the futon.

cards.context: Yotsuba goes shopping with Koiwai and the Ayase family. N3 learners know this word but sometimes falter on 物 readings (もの vs もの in compounds).
cards.example_sentence: よつばとジャンボで買い物に行くことにした。
cards.example_reading: よつば と じゃんぼ で かいもの に いく こと に した。
cards.example_meaning: We decided to go shopping with Yotsuba and Jumbo.

cards.context: A key activity across volumes 2 and 3. This compound is transparent once you know 虫（むし）and 取る（とる）, but learners often don't connect the pieces in kanji form.
cards.example_sentence: 虫取りに行こう！網持ってきた？
cards.example_reading: むしとり に いこう！あみ もって きた？
cards.example_meaning: Let's go bug catching! Did you bring the net?

cards.simpler_synonym: なし（日本固有の夏の虫）
cards.context: Summer chapters are defined by cicada sounds and catching them. Written in katakana in the manga. Even if learners know the word they may not know the cultural weight — cicadas signal summer in Japan.
cards.example_sentence: セミがうるさいくらい鳴いている。
cards.example_reading: せみ が うるさい くらい ないて いる。
cards.example_meaning: The cicadas are crying so loud it's almost too much.

cards.context: An entire volume arc is set at an amusement park. The word is made of logical parts (遊＋園＋地) but the compound itself is its own vocabulary item.
cards.example_sentence: 初めて遊園地に来た！すごい！
cards.example_reading: はじめて ゆうえんち に きた！すごい！
cards.example_meaning: I came to an amusement park for the first time! Amazing!

cards.context: Appears when Yotsuba visits Fuuka's grandmother's house in the countryside. Helps understand the rural-vs-city contrast the manga uses.
cards.example_sentence: ここは農家だから野菜が新鮮だよ。
cards.example_reading: ここ は のうか だ から やさい が しんせん だよ。
cards.example_meaning: This is a farming household so the vegetables are fresh.

cards.context: Included because N3 learners sometimes confuse 歩く（あるく）with 散歩（さんぽ）in nuance — 散歩 is a leisure stroll, not just walking.
cards.example_sentence: よつば、散歩に行くぞ。
cards.example_reading: よつば、さんぽ に いくぞ。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba, we're going for a walk.

cards.simpler_synonym: 次の日（つぎのひ）、明日（あした）
cards.context: Used in narrative transitions between chapters. N3 learners know 明日 but often don't recognise the more formal 翌日 in captions.
cards.example_sentence: 翌日の朝、よつばは早起きした。
cards.example_reading: よくじつ の あさ、よつば は はやおき した。
cards.example_meaning: The following morning, Yotsuba woke up early.

cards.context: Appears in background description of the suburban street setting. Yotsuba notices them. The compound 電線 is straightforward (電＋線) for learners who know both kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 電線にカラスが止まっている。
cards.example_reading: でんせん に からす が とまって いる。
cards.example_meaning: A crow is perched on the power line.

cards.context: Yotsuba learns to ride a bicycle. This compound (自＋転＋車) has three kanji with readings N3 learners may not have fully fixed — worth drilling the reading as a whole word.
cards.example_sentence: よつばは自転車に乗れるようになった！
cards.example_reading: よつば は じてんしゃ に のれる ように なった！
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba has become able to ride a bicycle!

cards.context: Appears in grocery and breakfast scenes. N3 learners often know the word but confuse 牛（ぎゅう）with 牛（うし）and 乳（にゅう）vs 乳（ちち）readings.
cards.example_sentence: 朝は牛乳を飲むといいぞ。
cards.example_reading: あさ は ぎゅうにゅう を のむ と いいぞ。
cards.example_meaning: Drinking milk in the morning is good for you.

meanings: to make a racket from excitement
cards.simpler_synonym: 大はしゃぎする、喜びすぎる
cards.context: Perfectly describes Yotsuba's typical behaviour everywhere. This verb is very common in descriptions of children or excitable characters in manga.
cards.example_sentence: よつばははしゃいで庭を走り回った。
cards.example_reading: よつば は はしゃいで にわ を はしりまわった。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba was excitedly running around the garden.

cards.context: Used to describe a character staring into space or thinking vaguely. Adult characters (especially Koiwai) often 'ぼんやりする' in contrast to Yotsuba's energy.
cards.example_sentence: お父さんはぼんやりと空を見上げていた。
cards.example_reading: おとうさん は ぼんやり と そら を みあげて いた。
cards.example_meaning: Dad was staring up at the sky absent-mindedly.

cards.simpler_synonym: 歩き回る（あるきまわる）
cards.context: Yotsuba うろうろs constantly — in the new neighbourhood, in shops, at events. This mimetic word will appear in almost every volume.
cards.example_sentence: よつばが知らない道をうろうろしていた。
cards.example_reading: よつば が しらない みち を うろうろ して いた。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba was wandering around on an unfamiliar street.

cards.context: Yotsuba's default state. This mimetic word pairs constantly with する: わくわくする. N3 learners often know it but don't recognise it in context without the する.
cards.example_sentence: 明日の遠足がわくわくする！
cards.example_reading: あした の えんそく が わくわく する！
cards.example_meaning: I'm so excited about tomorrow's field trip!

cards.context: Used for moments of nervous excitement — Yotsuba at the amusement park, or when someone is waiting for something scary/exciting.
cards.example_sentence: お化け屋敷の前でどきどきしてきた。
cards.example_reading: おばけやしき の まえ で どきどき して きた。
cards.example_meaning: My heart started pounding in front of the haunted house.

cards.simpler_synonym: きれいに光っている、新品
cards.context: Used when describing things that are very clean or new. Yotsuba uses it to describe things she finds impressively shiny or pristine.
cards.example_sentence: よつばの靴はぴかぴかだ。
cards.example_reading: よつば の くつ は ぴかぴか だ。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba's shoes are gleaming clean.

cards.simpler_synonym: くるくる（似たニュアンス）、回る（まわる）
cards.context: Appears for spinning rides at the amusement park and for Yotsuba twirling. The distinction between ぐるぐる (bigger/dizzying) and くるくる (smaller/cuter) is a useful nuance.
cards.example_sentence: メリーゴーランドがぐるぐる回っている。
cards.example_reading: めりーごーらんど が ぐるぐる まわって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The merry-go-round is spinning round and round.

cards.context: The Ayase sisters くすくす when Yotsuba does something unexpectedly funny. Useful for distinguishing different types of laughter in manga SFX.
cards.example_sentence: あさぎはくすくすと笑った。
cards.example_reading: あさぎ は くすくす と わらった。
cards.example_meaning: Asagi giggled softly.

cards.context: Often written in hiragana in the manga (いたずら) but the kanji form 悪戯 also appears occasionally. Yanda is described as いたずらっ子.
cards.example_sentence: ヤンダはよつばにいたずらばかりする。
cards.example_reading: やんだ は よつば に いたずら ばかり する。
cards.example_meaning: Yanda does nothing but play tricks on Yotsuba.

meanings: to be mad (おこる = colloquial; いかる = formal/literary)
cards.simpler_synonym: 腹を立てる（はらをたてる）
cards.context: Koiwai and the Ayase mother 怒る Yotsuba frequently. The two readings (おこる for casual use, いかる for literary/formal) confuse learners — in this manga it's always おこる.
cards.example_sentence: よつばが怒ったって顔してる。
cards.example_reading: よつば が おこった って かお してる。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba's got an 'I'm angry' face on.

cards.context: Yotsuba is made to apologise in several scenes. The kanji 謝 is also the 謝 in 感謝（かんしゃ）— connecting them helps retention.
cards.example_sentence: ちゃんと謝りなさい！
cards.example_reading: ちゃんと あやまりなさい！
cards.example_meaning: Apologise properly!

cards.context: Yotsuba shows visible disappointment when plans fall through. Used as both an adverb (がっかりした顔) and verb phrase (がっかりする).
cards.example_sentence: 雨でキャンプが中止になってよつばはがっかりした。
cards.example_reading: あめ で きゃんぷ が ちゅうし に なって よつば は がっかり した。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba was disappointed that the camp was cancelled because of rain.

cards.simpler_synonym: 友達（ともだち）、仲がいい
cards.context: Written both as 仲良し and なかよし. The kanji form surprises learners who only know the hiragana. Yotsuba rapidly becomes なかよし with all the neighbours.
cards.example_sentence: よつばとあさぎはすぐなかよしになった。
cards.example_reading: よつば と あさぎ は すぐ なかよし に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba and Asagi quickly became good friends.

cards.simpler_synonym: 他の人の（ほかのひとの）
cards.context: よその子、よその家 — appears when adults remind Yotsuba of boundaries between her own home and neighbours'. A culturally loaded term about in-group vs out-group.
cards.example_sentence: よその家に勝手に入ってはいけないよ。
cards.example_reading: よそ の いえ に かってに はいって は いけない よ。
cards.example_meaning: You mustn't go into someone else's house without asking.

cards.simpler_synonym: すごい、かわいい（※女性に使う場合）
cards.context: Yotsuba calls Jumbo and others かっこいい. The word comes from 格好（かっこう）+ いい but is only written in kana in colloquial use. N3 learners sometimes don't know the kanji origin.
cards.example_sentence: ジャンボはかっこいいな！
cards.example_reading: じゃんぼ は かっこいい な！
cards.example_meaning: Jumbo is so cool!

cards.simpler_synonym: 馬鹿にする、見下す（みくだす）
cards.context: Yotsuba accuses Yanda of ばかにする-ing her. The expression is colloquial and written in kana or kanji in the manga.
cards.example_sentence: ヤンダ、よつばのことばかにしてる！
cards.example_reading: やんだ、よつば の こと ばかに してる！
cards.example_meaning: Yanda is making fun of Yotsuba!

cards.simpler_synonym: うん、と言う、頭を縦に振る
cards.context: Often written in hiragana in manga. The kanji form 頷く is rarely used but exists. Appears in narrator captions when Yotsuba or other characters agree silently.
cards.example_sentence: よつばは大きくうなずいた。
cards.example_reading: よつば は おおきく うなずいた。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba gave a big nod.

cards.context: Referenced in early volumes when Koiwai's lifestyle is being established. The compound 暮らし（ぐらし）is an important suffix to know as it appears in many compounds.
cards.example_sentence: お父さんは前は一人暮らしだった。
cards.example_reading: おとうさん は まえ は ひとりぐらし だった。
cards.example_meaning: Dad used to live alone.

cards.context: Used constantly in child-directed speech. The polite prefix お + 出かけ. N3 learners know 出かける but may not recognise the noun form おでかけ.
cards.example_sentence: 今日はどこにおでかけするの？
cards.example_reading: きょう は どこ に おでかけ する の？
cards.example_meaning: Where are we going today?

cards.context: Appears in countryside scenes and in Yotsuba's toy pinwheels. Note that the toy pinwheel version is often called かざぐるま (風車 with different reading) — same kanji, different reading.
cards.example_sentence: 遠くに大きな風車が見える。
cards.example_reading: とおく に おおきな ふうしゃ が みえる。
cards.example_meaning: You can see a large windmill in the distance.

cards.context: The neighbourhood shrine features in several scenes. The reading じんじゃ is straightforward but the kanji 社（しゃ）has multiple readings that trip N3 learners.
cards.example_sentence: 神社の前で記念写真を撮った。
cards.example_reading: じんじゃ の まえ で きねんしゃしん を とった。
cards.example_meaning: We took a commemorative photo in front of the shrine.

cards.simpler_synonym: なし（これが普通の言い方）
cards.context: Included because N3 learners sometimes confuse 公園（こうえん）with 公演（こうえん = public performance) — homophones. Context in Yotsuba always means park.
cards.example_sentence: 公園でブランコに乗ろう！
cards.example_reading: こうえん で ぶらんこ に のろう！
cards.example_meaning: Let's ride the swings at the park!

cards.context: Yotsuba is fascinated by frogs and tries to catch them. Written in katakana. The homophones 帰る（かえる = to go home）and 変える（かえる = to change）cause confusion for learners.
cards.example_sentence: あ！カエルがいる！つかまえよう！
cards.example_reading: あ！かえる が いる！つかまえよう！
cards.example_meaning: Oh! There's a frog! Let's catch it!

cards.context: Culturally specific summer activity. Appears in summer chapters when characters sit outside in the evening. Beautiful word — worth knowing for cultural literacy even if JLPT-hard.
cards.example_sentence: 縁側で夕涼みしながらスイカを食べた。
cards.example_reading: えんがわ で ゆうすずみ しながら すいか を たべた。
cards.example_meaning: We ate watermelon on the veranda while enjoying the cool evening air.

meanings: I have a request (used as exclamation)
cards.context: Yotsuba uses this in its exclamatory form constantly. N3 learners know お願いします but may not recognise the standalone おねがい！ as a pleading particle in manga speech bubbles.
cards.example_sentence: ねーお父さん、おねがい！買って！
cards.example_reading: ねー おとうさん、おねがい！かって！
cards.example_meaning: Daaad, please! Buy it for me!

meanings: I don't know what to do
cards.context: A very frequent expression in moments of panic or indecision. Appears almost every time Yotsuba or another character is in a fix. Must be recognised instantly.
cards.example_sentence: どうしよう！財布を忘れた！
cards.example_reading: どうしよう！さいふ を わすれた！
cards.example_meaning: What do I do! I forgot my wallet!

cards.context: One of the most common discourse words in casual Japanese. Yotsuba uses it to confirm her suspicions. Also appears as やっぱ in very casual speech in the manga.
cards.example_sentence: やっぱりアイスは最高だ！
cards.example_reading: やっぱり あいす は さいこう だ！
cards.example_meaning: As I thought, ice cream is the best!

cards.context: Extremely frequent in the manga as characters constantly point things out to Yotsuba. N3 learners often know it but miss it in fast-paced dialogue because it can stand alone in a speech bubble.
cards.example_sentence: ほら、あそこにセミがいるよ！
cards.example_reading: ほら、あそこ に せみ が いるよ！
cards.example_meaning: Look, there's a cicada over there!

cards.context: A culturally key Japanese concept. Appears when characters scold Yotsuba for wasting food or resources. The word is often written in kana in the manga.
cards.example_sentence: 食べ物を残すなんてもったいない！
cards.example_reading: たべもの を のこす なんて もったいない！
cards.example_meaning: Leaving food uneaten — what a waste!

cards.context: Used by Koiwai and Jumbo. Colloquial contraction of 面倒くさい. N3 learners may not connect めんどくさい to 面倒 — linking them is important.
cards.example_sentence: 料理はめんどくさいからカレーにしよう。
cards.example_reading: りょうり は めんどくさい から かれー に しよう。
cards.example_meaning: Cooking is such a bother, let's just do curry.

cards.context: Yotsuba gets びっくりした constantly. This mimetic word is used both as a noun (びっくりした顔) and verb phrase (びっくりする). Very high frequency.
cards.example_sentence: 急に大声を出してびっくりした！
cards.example_reading: きゅうに おおごえ を だして びっくりした！
cards.example_meaning: You shouted so suddenly — I was startled!

cards.simpler_synonym: 楽しい（たのしい）※やや違う
cards.context: Included because the kanji form 嬉しい uses an uncommon character. N3 learners know the word in kana but often miss it in the rare cases it appears in kanji in captions.
cards.example_sentence: プレゼントをもらってよつばはとてもうれしかった。
cards.example_reading: ぷれぜんと を もらって よつば は とても うれしかった。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuba was very happy to receive a present.

cards.context: Adult characters 困る very frequently when Yotsuba does something unexpected. The expression 困ったな / 困ったね is a set phrase for mild exasperation.
cards.example_sentence: よつばが迷子になって本当に困った。
cards.example_reading: よつば が まいご に なって ほんとうに こまった。
cards.example_meaning: I was really at a loss when Yotsuba got lost.

cards.context: Used in scenes where the group is running late. The imperative form 急げ！ (hurry up!) appears in manga in action panels.
cards.example_sentence: 急いで！バスが来るよ！
cards.example_reading: いそいで！ばす が くる よ！
cards.example_meaning: Hurry up! The bus is coming!

cards.simpler_synonym: 遠慮しないで = 気にしないで
cards.context: Appears in polite exchanges. 遠慮なく（えんりょなく）means 'don't hold back / help yourself'. N3 learners often encounter 遠慮なく at meals but don't know the source word.
cards.example_sentence: 遠慮しないで食べてね。
cards.example_reading: えんりょ しないで たべて ね。
cards.example_meaning: Don't hold back — eat as much as you like.

cards.context: Used when preparing for outings, meals, or activities. 用意はいい？ ('Are you ready?') is a very common phrase in the manga.
cards.example_sentence: キャンプの用意はできた？
cards.example_reading: きゃんぷ の ようい は できた？
cards.example_meaning: Are you ready / are the preparations done for camping?

cards.simpler_synonym: 注意して（ちゅういして）
cards.context: Said constantly by adult characters when Yotsuba goes off on adventures. The base verb 気をつける is important to learn separately from its te-form usage.
cards.example_sentence: 一人で行くなら気をつけてね。
cards.example_reading: ひとり で いく なら きを つけてね。
cards.example_meaning: If you're going alone, take care.

cards.context: The rough imperative of やめる. Used by Koiwai and Jumbo. N3 learners should understand that やめて is softer (request) while やめろ is a firm command — the register difference matters in manga.
cards.example_sentence: コイワイ、それやめろよ！
cards.example_reading: こいわい、それ やめろ よ！
cards.example_meaning: Koiwai, cut that out!

cards.simpler_synonym: 問題ない（もんだいない）
cards.context: Included because the kanji 丈 is uncommon. In modern usage 大丈夫 can also mean 'No thank you' when used as a refusal — an important colloquial evolution that confuses learners.
cards.example_sentence: 転んだ？大丈夫？
cards.example_reading: ころんだ？だいじょうぶ？
cards.example_meaning: Did you fall? Are you OK?

cards.simpler_synonym: なし（このままの形で使う）
cards.context: A discourse marker that signals a change of topic or a recalled thought. Characters use it frequently in conversation. N3 learners often parse this as そう + いえば and miss the idiomatic meaning.
cards.example_sentence: そういえば、昨日ジャンボが来たんだって。
cards.example_reading: そういえば、きのう じゃんぼ が きたん だって。
cards.example_meaning: Come to think of it, apparently Jumbo came by yesterday.

cards.context: Yotsuba's most frequently asked question. The casual equivalent of なぜ/どうして. N3 learners who have learned textbook Japanese may not recognise なんで as the primary 'why' in spoken/manga Japanese.
cards.example_sentence: なんでよつばだけダメなの！
cards.example_reading: なんで よつば だけ だめ な の！
cards.example_meaning: How come only Yotsuba can't do it!

cards.context: Used by adults constantly to tell Yotsuba to do things properly. ちゃんとしなさい is a key parenting phrase. Nuance: ちゃんと emphasises meeting a standard, not just 'carefully'.
cards.example_sentence: ちゃんと手を洗った？
cards.example_reading: ちゃんと て を あらった？
cards.example_meaning: Did you wash your hands properly?

cards.simpler_synonym: なし（文脈で意味が変わる）
cards.context: Koiwai uses まあ frequently. It softens statements, expresses mild resignation, or fills a pause. Untranslatable directly — context is everything. N3 learners often overlook it.
cards.example_sentence: まあ、仕方ないか。
cards.example_reading: まあ、しかたない か。
cards.example_meaning: Well... I guess it can't be helped.

cards.context: The double-t ending (っ) indicates a sharper, more surprised reaction than え?. Recognising the difference between え, えっ, えー, ええっ is important for reading emotional tone in manga.
cards.example_sentence: えっ、もう終わり？
cards.example_reading: えっ、もう おわり？
cards.example_meaning: Huh? Already over?

cards.simpler_synonym: 素晴らしい（すばらしい）
cards.context: Yotsuba's go-to exclamation for everything impressive. N3 learners know this, but the manga also uses すごい as an adverb (すごい大きい = すごく大きい) — a colloquial feature textbooks don't always teach.
cards.example_sentence: すごい！こんな大きい虫初めて見た！
cards.example_reading: すごい！こんな おおきい むし はじめて みた！
cards.example_meaning: Amazing! I've never seen such a big bug before!
